exposure: Maternal pre-pregnancy overweight/obesity (categorised according to WHO)
outcome: Mode of delivery (vaginal vs. emergency caesarean section)
cohort: The study included 4859 women (1987 first-generation immigrants, 687 second-generation immigrants, and 2185 non-immigrants) from Berlin, Germany, aged 18+ years with gestational age 24+ weeks.
finding: Maternal pre-pregnancy overweight and obesity were associated with an elevated risk of labour induction and emergency caesarean section, irrespective of the woman's migrant status.
mod_finding: Obese women were more likely to have their labour induced and to deliver by emergency caesarean section compared to normal weight women, regardless of migrant status.
